summary: SessionBoard Abstract Management runs the academic-style submission lifecycle end-to-end. Organizers build custom submission forms per category (papers, posters, panels) with flexible fields, conditional logic, file uploads, and optional submission payments (100+ gateways, promo codes, VAT). Authors submit abstracts and attach co-authors/presenters with custom participant roles (Author, Co-author, Panelist, Discussant), then track status. Review runs through Evaluation Plans containing multiple independent rounds (e.g. Initial Review, Final Review, Committee Decision), each with its own scorecard (numeric, dropdown, text, file-upload fields), open/close dates, anonymization settings (single/double blind), and reviewer pool. External reviewers access a branded portal via magic link — no accounts — where they read abstracts, score, and comment. AI Evaluators optionally provide first-pass numeric scores with reasoning via configurable reviewer personas; humans can override. Chairs monitor a real-time progress dashboard, send bulk reminders, view aggregate scores, and record dispositions (accept, reject, waitlist, request revision). Automated notifications inform submitters at each stage. Accepted abstracts convert to sessions with metadata intact, flowing directly into the agenda builder, speaker portal, and content management — no re-entry. Reporting includes natural-language queries, shareable dashboards, exports, and a full submission-to-agenda audit trail.
personas: Organizer/program chair (admin): builds forms, configures evaluation plans, assigns reviewers, monitors progress, records dispositions, builds program
Submitter/author: completes submission form, adds co-authors, tracks status, edits/withdraws
Co-author/presenter: listed on submission with a role (Author, Co-author, Panelist, Discussant)
Reviewer: external, enters via magic-link portal, scores and comments on assigned abstracts
Committee member: views aggregate scores and reviewer comments to make final decisions

user_journeys.name: Author submits an abstract with co-authors
steps: Open the event's public abstract submission page
Choose submission type/track (e.g. Research Paper vs Poster) — form fields adjust via conditional logic
Fill title (required), abstract body, custom fields (keywords, track dropdown), upload supporting file
Add co-authors with name/email and assign roles (Co-author, Presenter)
Pay submission fee if configured (or apply promo code)
Submit and land on confirmation; submission appears in author's dashboard with status 'Submitted'
user_journeys.filled_state: Author dashboard listing 1-3 submissions with titles, types, statuses (Submitted / Under Review / Accepted), each detail view showing abstract text, uploaded file, and a participants list with roles

user_journeys.name: Chair configures a multi-round evaluation plan
steps: Open review/evaluation settings and create an Evaluation Plan
Add Round 1 'Initial Review' with open/close dates, double-blind anonymization, and a scorecard (numeric 1-5 Originality, dropdown Recommendation, text Comments)
Add Round 2 'Final Review' with a different scorecard and reviewer pool
Assign submissions to reviewers by track, set per-reviewer limits, preview assignments, confirm
Optionally enable an AI Evaluator persona for first-pass scoring
user_journeys.filled_state: Evaluation plan screen showing 2+ named rounds with distinct dates, scorecards, anonymization flags, and reviewer pools; assignment matrix showing reviewers with counts of assigned submissions

user_journeys.name: Reviewer scores assigned abstracts via portal
steps: Open reviewer portal via magic link (no password/account)
See queue of assigned abstracts with completion status
Open an abstract — author names hidden if round is blinded
Fill scorecard: numeric ratings, dropdown recommendation, text comments
Submit evaluation; item marked complete in queue
user_journeys.filled_state: Reviewer dashboard with 4-6 assigned abstracts, 2 marked complete with scores visible, remaining pending; open review showing filled scorecard

user_journeys.name: Chair reviews scores, decides, and builds the program
steps: Open progress dashboard: per-reviewer/per-round completion rates; send bulk reminders to laggards
Open results view with aggregate scores per submission (human + AI, with AI reasoning)
Set dispositions: Accept, Reject, Waitlist, or Request Revision; personalized notifications fire
Accepted abstracts convert to sessions with metadata intact and appear in the agenda builder
Accepted speakers auto-invited to speaker portal
user_journeys.filled_state: Results table of 8-10 submissions with average scores, reviewer counts, disposition badges in mixed states; agenda builder showing accepted sessions with titles/speakers carried over

features.name: Custom submission forms
features.description: Custom forms with flexible fields, conditional logic, file uploads; different form types per submission category (research paper, poster, panel). Title is the only required field; description optional.
features.ui_expectations: Admin form builder (add/reorder fields, field types, branching rules); public-facing submission form with text inputs, dropdowns, file upload, conditional fields that appear/disappear

features.name: Co-author and participant roles
features.description: Collect authors, co-authors, and presenters directly in the form with custom participant roles: Author, Co-author, Panelist, Discussant, or any custom label. Multiple participants per submission.
features.ui_expectations: Add-participant control within submission form; participants list on submission detail showing name, email, role badge

features.name: Submitter status tracking, edit and withdraw
features.description: Authors track submission status and receive updates at every stage; can edit submissions and withdraw before/until review begins (inferred from category norms).
features.ui_expectations: Author dashboard listing submissions with status labels (Submitted, Under Review, Accepted, Rejected, Withdrawn); edit and withdraw actions on own submissions

features.name: Multi-round evaluation plans
features.description: Each evaluation plan contains multiple independent rounds (Initial Review, Final Review, Committee Decision); each round has its own scorecard, open/close dates, anonymization settings, and reviewer pool.
features.ui_expectations: Admin evaluation-plan screen with named rounds, per-round date pickers, scorecard selector, anonymization toggle, reviewer-pool picker

features.name: Configurable scorecards
features.description: Scorecard fields support numeric ratings, dropdown-based scoring, qualitative text feedback, and file uploads; scoring rubrics can vary by session/submission type.
features.ui_expectations: Scorecard editor with field types; reviewer-side rendering of numeric scales, dropdowns, text areas

features.name: Reviewer assignment
features.description: Assign specific submissions to specific reviewers, filter/assign by track, set per-reviewer review limits, preview assignments before confirming.
features.ui_expectations: Assignment screen: multi-select submissions, pick reviewer(s), limit setting, assignment preview, confirm action

features.name: Reviewer portal (magic link)
features.description: Reviewers access a dedicated branded review dashboard via magic link — no admin account or password — where they read abstracts, apply scores, and leave comments.
features.ui_expectations: Passwordless entry link; reviewer queue with pending/complete indicators; abstract reading pane plus scorecard side-by-side

features.name: Anonymization / blind review
features.description: Single-blind or double-blind anonymization, configurable per review round; blinded reviewers cannot see author identity or other reviewers' evaluations.
features.ui_expectations: Per-round anonymization setting; reviewer view with author names/affiliations stripped when enabled

features.name: Review progress dashboard
features.description: Real-time dashboard: which reviewers are on track, which rounds are open, completion rates; bulk reminders to reviewers with outstanding assignments.
features.ui_expectations: Progress metrics per reviewer and per round (completed/pending counts or percentages); select-and-remind bulk action

features.name: AI Evaluators
features.description: AI first-pass scoring of every submission: numeric score with reasoning and contextual notes; configurable reviewer personas with weighted criteria (originality, expertise, audience value); humans can override AI scores; evaluation activity logged.
features.ui_expectations: AI score with rationale text on submission; persona configuration; override control for admins/reviewers

features.name: Disposition and decisions
features.description: Committee views aggregate scoring data and reviewer comments to make selections; submissions are accepted, rejected, waitlisted, or sent back for revision; decisions logged.
features.ui_expectations: Results table with aggregate/average scores per submission; disposition controls (Accept/Reject/Waitlist/Revise); status badges that persist

features.name: Automated stage notifications
features.description: Automated communications at each stage: submission confirmations, status update notifications when decisions are made, personalized acceptance/rejection messages triggered by workflow, reviewer reminders.
features.ui_expectations: Notification/email template settings tied to decision events; visible confirmation after submission

features.name: Abstract-to-session conversion
features.description: Accepted abstracts become sessions with all metadata intact — no re-entry — flowing directly into the agenda builder, speaker portal, and content management; multiple abstracts can combine into a single finalized session.
features.ui_expectations: Convert/promote action or automatic flow on acceptance; agenda/program builder listing sessions with carried-over title, description, speakers

features.name: Submission payments
features.description: Payments handled natively within the submission form; 100+ payment gateways, promo codes for invited speakers/committee, VAT configuration; PCI-compliant, no card data stored.
features.ui_expectations: Payment step in submission flow with price display, promo-code field that adjusts total, gateway checkout

features.name: Reporting and analytics
features.description: Natural-language report queries, custom dashboards built from prompts, shareable password-protected reports with access logs, exportable reports on real-time submission and reviewer data.
features.ui_expectations: Reports area with a submissions/scores table view; share/export controls; optional NL query box

features.name: Audit trail
features.description: Full submission-to-agenda audit trail: every stage and decision permanently logged; all evaluation activity logged for accountability.
features.ui_expectations: History/activity log on a submission showing timestamped stage changes and decisions

rubric.criterion: Author can submit an abstract through a public form with title, abstract body, and at least one custom field, and receive confirmation
auto_steps: Navigate to the clone's CFP/abstract submission page
Start a new submission; select a type/track if offered
Fill title 'Transformer Efficiency in Low-Power Edge Devices', abstract body (2-3 sentences), and any custom fields (keywords, track dropdown)
Submit the form
Open the author's submissions list/dashboard
rubric.pass_criteria: Submission is accepted without error; confirmation shown; submission appears in author's list with correct title and a status label
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of filled form pre-submit, confirmation screen, and author dashboard row with the new submission

rubric.criterion: Admin form builder supports adding fields and conditional logic that changes the live form
auto_steps: Log in as admin and open the submission form builder
Add a dropdown field 'Format' with options Talk/Poster
Add a conditional rule: show a text field 'Poster dimensions' only when Format=Poster
Save; open the public form
Toggle Format between Talk and Poster and observe the dependent field
rubric.pass_criteria: Dependent field appears only when the triggering option is selected; configuration persists after save
rubric.evidence: Screenshots of the builder rule and the live form in both states (field hidden vs shown)

rubric.criterion: Submitter can add co-authors/participants with distinct roles and they persist on the submission
auto_steps: Start or edit a submission
Add participant 'Dana Wu, dana@example.com' with role Co-author and 'Prof. Ade Okafor' with role Discussant (or nearest available roles)
Submit/save
Open submission detail as author and as admin
rubric.pass_criteria: Both participants listed on the submission with their names and role labels in both views
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of the submission detail participants list showing names and roles

rubric.criterion: Author can see submission status, edit a pending submission, and withdraw one
auto_steps: As author open 'My submissions'
Verify each row shows a status label
Edit one submission's title (append ' v2') and save; reopen to confirm persistence
Trigger withdraw on a second test submission and confirm
rubric.pass_criteria: Edited title persists; withdrawn submission shows Withdrawn (or equivalent) status and is excluded from active review
rubric.evidence: Before/after screenshots of the edited title and the status change to Withdrawn

rubric.criterion: Admin can configure an evaluation plan with 2+ independent rounds, each with its own scorecard, open/close dates, and reviewer pool
auto_steps: As admin open review/evaluation settings
Create round 'Initial Review' with a date range, scorecard A, reviewer pool of 2 reviewers
Create round 'Final Review' with different dates, scorecard B, different pool
Save and reopen the plan
rubric.pass_criteria: Both rounds persist with visibly distinct scorecards, date ranges, and reviewer pools
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of the saved plan listing both rounds with their differing configurations

rubric.criterion: Scorecard editor supports numeric rating, dropdown, and free-text fields, and all three render for reviewers
auto_steps: As admin open scorecard editor
Add numeric 1-5 field 'Originality', dropdown 'Recommendation' (Accept/Maybe/Reject), long-text 'Comments'
Save; open a review as a reviewer
Enter values in all three fields and submit
rubric.pass_criteria: All three field types render on the reviewer side, accept input, and the submitted evaluation stores the values
rubric.evidence: Screenshots of scorecard editor and a completed reviewer evaluation showing all three values

rubric.criterion: Admin can assign specific submissions to a specific reviewer and the reviewer's queue reflects exactly those assignments
auto_steps: As admin open reviewer assignment
Select 2 of 5+ submissions and assign to reviewer R (set per-reviewer limit or track filter if offered)
Confirm assignments
Open reviewer R's queue/portal view
rubric.pass_criteria: Reviewer R sees exactly the assigned submissions (the 2 assigned, not the unassigned ones)
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of admin assignment state and reviewer R's queue listing only assigned items

rubric.criterion: Reviewer works in a dedicated portal — reads abstract, scores, comments, submits — via passwordless/magic-link style access
auto_steps: As admin locate/copy the reviewer's access link (or impersonate/open reviewer view)
Open it in a fresh browser context; note whether a password is demanded
Open an assigned abstract, fill the scorecard, add a comment, submit
Verify the item is marked complete in the queue
rubric.pass_criteria: Reviewer can complete an evaluation end-to-end without creating an account; completion state updates. Unverified automatically: delivery of the magic link by email — human confirms the invite email contains a working login-free link
rubric.evidence: Screenshots of reviewer dashboard, filled scorecard, and completed status; note on whether access required a password

rubric.criterion: With anonymization enabled for a round, the reviewer view hides author/co-author identity and other reviewers' scores
auto_steps: As admin enable double-blind (or blinded review) on a round
Open a submission in the reviewer view
Scan the page for the known author and co-author names and affiliation
Check that no other reviewer's scores/comments are displayed
rubric.pass_criteria: Author identity absent from blinded reviewer view while visible in admin view. Unverified automatically: cross-reviewer score isolation with a genuine second account — human logs in as a second reviewer to confirm they cannot see reviewer one's scores
rubric.evidence: Side-by-side screenshots: admin view showing author names vs blinded reviewer view without them

rubric.criterion: AI evaluator produces a first-pass numeric score with written reasoning on a submission, and a human can override it
auto_steps: Enable or run the AI evaluator on at least one submission (configure a persona if required)
Open the submission's evaluation view
Verify a numeric score plus rationale text attributed to the AI
Override/adjust the score as admin and save
rubric.pass_criteria: AI score and reasoning display; overridden value persists and is distinguishable from the AI's original. Unverified automatically: quality/consistency of AI reasoning
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of AI score with rationale and of the overridden score state

rubric.criterion: Admin sees aggregate scores per submission and can set dispositions (accept, reject, waitlist/revise) that persist
auto_steps: Complete 2+ reviewer evaluations on the same submission (or use seeded data)
Open the results/decisions view
Verify an aggregate (average/total) score is shown per submission
Set one submission Accepted, one Rejected, one Waitlisted or Revision-requested
Reload and verify statuses persist
rubric.pass_criteria: Aggregate score reflects the entered reviews; at least 3 distinct disposition states are available and persist after reload
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of results table with aggregate scores and mixed disposition badges after reload

rubric.criterion: Decision triggers a personalized acceptance/rejection notification to the submitter
rubric.pass_criteria: Human check: configure/enable decision notifications, mark one submission Accepted and one Rejected using submitter addresses you control; verify each inbox receives the correct decision email containing the submission title and matching disposition (and no cross-leak of the other decision)
rubric.evidence: Email receipts showing correct disposition, submission title, and recipient

rubric.criterion: Accepted abstract converts into a session in the agenda/program builder with metadata (title, description, speakers) intact and no re-entry
auto_steps: Accept a submission with known title, description, and participants
Trigger convert-to-session if not automatic
Open the agenda/program builder
Locate the session and compare title, description, and speaker names to the source abstract
rubric.pass_criteria: Session exists in the program area with matching title, description, and speakers without manual re-typing
rubric.evidence: Screenshots of the accepted abstract and the resulting session in the agenda builder with matching fields

rubric.criterion: Progress dashboard shows per-reviewer/per-round completion and offers bulk reminders to reviewers with outstanding reviews
auto_steps: Seed state: one reviewer complete, one with pending reviews
Open the review progress dashboard
Verify completion counts/percentages per reviewer (and per round if shown)
Select the lagging reviewer and trigger 'send reminder'; capture the confirmation
rubric.pass_criteria: Completion metrics match actual review state; reminder action confirms sending. Unverified automatically: reminder email delivery — human checks the reviewer inbox
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of progress metrics and the reminder-sent confirmation

rubric.criterion: Submission flow includes a payment step with a promo-code field that adjusts the total
auto_steps: Configure a paid submission type (or use seeded config) with a promo code, e.g. SPEAKER100
Proceed through the submission flow to the payment step
Verify price display; enter the promo code and apply
Verify the total updates; stop before any real payment
rubric.pass_criteria: Payment step renders with correct price; promo code changes the total. Unverified automatically: actual gateway charge — human completes a test-mode transaction to confirm end-to-end processing
rubric.evidence: Screenshots of payment step before and after promo application

rubric.criterion: A submissions report/table with statuses and scores can be generated and viewed
auto_steps: Open the reports/analytics area
Generate or open a submissions report including status and score columns
Verify rows match known seeded submissions
rubric.pass_criteria: Report renders with per-submission status and score data consistent with the underlying submissions
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of the report table with status and score columns populated

sample_data: Event: 'EdTech Research Summit 2026', CFP open, tracks: 'AI in Education', 'Learning Analytics', 'Teaching Practice'. Submission types: Research Paper, Poster, Panel (Poster conditionally shows 'Poster dimensions' field). 8 abstracts, e.g.: 'Transformer Efficiency in Low-Power Edge Devices' (author Maya Chen, co-author Dana Wu, role Co-author), 'Adaptive Quizzing at Scale' (author Luis Ortega, panelist Priya Nair), 'Ethics of Predictive Grading' (author Prof. Ade Okafor, discussant Sam Field), plus 5 more spread across tracks; 1 pre-withdrawn. Participant roles: Author, Co-author, Panelist, Discussant. Reviewers: 3 (rev1@example.com, rev2@example.com, rev3@example.com); rev1 assigned 3 abstracts (2 complete), rev2 assigned 3 (0 complete), rev3 pool for round 2. Evaluation plan: Round 1 'Initial Review' (double-blind, scorecard: Originality 1-5, Relevance 1-5, Recommendation dropdown Accept/Maybe/Reject, Comments text), Round 2 'Final Review' (open dates later, scorecard: Final score 1-10, Comments). Dispositions seeded: 2 Accepted, 1 Rejected, 1 Waitlisted, rest pending. One paid submission type: Poster $25 with promo code SPEAKER100 (100% off). One accepted abstract already converted to session 'Adaptive Quizzing at Scale' in agenda builder.
gaps: Marketing pages omit specifics that were inferred from category norms (Sessionize/OpenReview/EasyChair/Cvent): exact disposition vocabulary (waitlist and revision-request implied but not shown as named statuses); submitter edit/withdraw rules and cutoffs (inferred); score aggregation method (average vs weighted — unspecified); conflict-of-interest declaration/recusal (not mentioned anywhere — excluded from rubric); revision round-trip mechanics (how a revised abstract re-enters review); mechanics of merging multiple abstracts into one session (stated as possible, no UI detail); reviewer magic-link expiry/security; per-reviewer limit UI specifics; whether AI Evaluator runs automatically or on demand. No screenshots were accessible via fetch (text-only extraction), so UI layout expectations are inferred from copy and category conventions.
